attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, describing a diagram he inspected.

semantics.note: A faithful observation about the first labeled bike diagram. 'Revealing' is Marcus's own gloss on why the errors matter; the contract rightly tests only the labeling errors.

contract.note: Reading 'several' as at least three distinct labeling errors is ordinary, and it matches the three examples Marcus gave. Requiring an inspectable image or an independent assessment is reasonable.

evidence.note: A secondary news summary that closely paraphrases Marcus's examples and shows no independent inspection or bicycle expertise. It cannot verify the labels.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no inspectable copy of the diagram and no independent qualified assessment. The only item repeats Marcus's account, and the speaker's own description cannot prove itself. No counterevidence was found either. The evidence available does not settle whether three or more labeling errors exist.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post about the tandem image he generated.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the tandem-image scope and the claim that knowledgeable cyclists would readily see numerous problems.

contract.note: Reading 'anybody' and 'immediately' as 'readily apparent' is fair. Excluding the bike's unusual height, which the prompt requested, is also fair. Requiring the image plus a qualified assessment is reasonable.

evidence.note: A same-day reader comment alleging missing left-side pedals. The reader's expertise is unverified, and the comment adds one alleged fault without verifying numerous faults.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no inspectable tandem image and no qualified independent review. The one reader comment is unverified context and alleges a single fault. Marcus's own descriptions cannot prove themselves, and no counterevidence was found. The evidence available does not settle the claim.
